question: In the border area between Egypt and Gaza, the Cairo authorities have constructed a prison town spanning 16 square kilometres, enclosed by walls seven metres high. This area is situated between the Rafah and Kerem Shalom crossings to the east, and the villages of Qoz Abo Raad and El-Masora to the west.

According to some sources, this prison city could potentially be used to accommodate tens of thousands of Palestinians if Israel decides to carry out a mass expulsion of the population from Rafah, where currently around 1.5 million displaced persons are concentrated. Considering that the European Union has announced an allocation of EUR 7.4 billion to Egypt, questions arise regarding the funding for this facility. 1.
Is the Commission aware of the construction of this prison city in Egypt?
How does the Commission plan to respond in the event of a mass deportation of the Palestinian population from Rafah?
Supporter1
This question is supported by a Member other than the authors:Rosa D'Amato(Verts/ALE)
answer: Subject: Direct or indirect links between the Commission and the buffer zone project at the Egyptian border with Gaza Sinai Foundation for Human Rights revealed video footage on 15 February 2024 showing that Egypt was building a buffer zone ‘ringed with high concrete walls along its border’ with the Gaza strip, between Al-Massoura and Rafah, suggesting that it could be used as an open air prison ‘with the aim of receiving refugees in the event of a mass exodus’.

Simultaneously, Israel is targeting Rafah where more than 1.5 million Palestinians are displaced, which could lead to a massive displacement of the Palestinian population towards Egypt. The Commission has announced that it will disburse a EUR 7.4 billion macro-financial assistance package to Egypt, notably due to its important role in the humanitarian context in the Gaza strip.
In the event that Egypt builds an open air prison to hold large numbers of deported Palestinians: 1.
Is the Commission in discussion with the Egyptian Government regarding this facility project?
What is the Commission doing to ensure that EU funds to Egypt are not directly or indirectly used to finance such a facility project?
What is the Commission doing to prevent the forced expulsion of Palestinians from the Gaza strip?

Joint answer given by Mr Várhelyi on behalf of the European Commission (1 July 2024) The Commission is not aware of such facility. The Strategic and Comprehensive Partnership with Egypt was launched with the signature of the Joint Declaration on 17 March 2024 (2). The joint declaration covers six key pillars: (1) political relations; (2) economic stability; (3) trade and investment; (4) migration and mobility; (5) security and (6) demography and human capital.

This question is supported by a Member other than the authors:Rosa D'Amato(Verts/ALE) https://neighbourhood-enlargement.ec.europa.eu/news/joint-declaration-strategic-and-comprehensive-partnership-between-arab-republic-egypt-and-european2024-03-17_en
A financial and investment support package of EUR 7.4 billion (3) has been announced to underpin the partnership. It will consist of short and longer-term support, covering the period 2024-2027.

This will include support to the macro-fiscal and socioeconomic reform agenda, as well as increased amounts to support investments in Egypt and targeted support through projects and technical assistance for the implementation of the different strategic priorities.

The Commission monitors its programmes through regular reports from implementing partners, external evaluation, verification missions and specific results-oriented monitoring exercises. The EU remains firmly committed to a lasting and sustainable peace in the Middle East based on the two-state solution as stated by the European Council in March 2024 (4).
